Broken promises: Northern Cape

By: Anina Peens | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
On the eve of the national election, we take a deep dive into the Northern Cape to look at what exactly the ANC government has done for the people.

Unique Selling Point:
How many broken buildings symbolise the governments' broken promises to its people?

Summary:
The Northern Cape... a forgotten province

Further information:
1. Kimberley Water
For over 20 years the Northern cape government has neglected to maintain the water system in Kimberley. Funding designated by national government was misused and mismanaged by both provincial and local government. The result? Knee high sewage running in people’s gardens and into their houses while drinking water is contaminated. Two wastewater treatment plants are completely rundown, and the entire system has now collapsed.
While government is securing over 3.5 billion Rand to resurrect the system, private business has stepped in for the rescue. Last weekend, Ekapa, a private mining company began work on two of six earmarked projects to clean the clarifiers of the system and secure drinking water for the interim.


2. Hopeless Hopetown
There seems to be countless unfinished projects in Hopetown. The community is fed up with local government that is never able to get anything done.
The local sports stadium: Two years ago, over 12 million was granted to build a sports stadium for the use of the community. The contractor was awarded the tender, illegally and only spent 800 thousand of the 12 million on the stadium. Today, there is barely anything left of the stadium. It has been vandalized and even monkeys and baboons have moved and destroyed what is left of it. A forensic investigation was completed by treasury but the local government refuses to table it. Those responsible for the wasteful expenditure are still in office.
The forensic report also investigated monies spent on the electrification of hillside, an informal settlement in Hopetown. People were moved to the settlement in 2014 and services were only given in 2018. But only partly… half of the community was left without electricity. Then came the 2021 elections and suddenly, it was a priority again. A contractor was awarded a tender to install electricity… but alas, a few poles were planted, without a proper spatial plan. There is no space for a proper road between the poles and there has been no electricity connected. After the election, the contractor was never seen again. The same culprits are implicated in the report and the ANC municipality refuses to table the report.
3. The De Aar Tunnels
In 2019, the department of Northern cape department of agriculture was given over 20 million Rand to establish a community vegetable tunnel outside De Aar. Feasibility studies conducted prior to erecting the tunnels indicated that it the project had no feasibility. Yet, government continued. Now, five years down the line, the website boasts that the tunnels are providing tonnes of cherry tomatoes to the export market but to the contrary, the tunnels have been vandalized to the bone. There is nothing left but a few odd poles representing another broken promise to community members who hoped for employment in a province with one of the highest unemployment rates. And no one is taking responsibility…

4. Philipstown/Petrusville/ Keurtjieskloof
- Another 12 million Rand given to a stadium that was never built in Keurtjieskloof. The contractor took off with the money and now baboons are living in the stadium while vandals are removing every last piece.
- The town hall in Keurtjieskloof was also supposed to be upgraded for the use of the community… nothing has happened.
- A brand-new school for Petrusville was initiated by premier Zimani Saul and millions were allocated for the project. Five years down the line and the school has still not been finished.
- A state funded piggery was established for the community of Philipstown. Millions were spent, but there is not one pig left, just vandalized office buildings.
- A contractor was hired two years ago to build a proper dumping site. He took two million Rand of the money and erected a windy house in an open field. That was it. Two years later, the same contractor was sworn in as municipal manager. It is alleged that he now sells sassa grants from his garage

text: Add New Proposal Shows Add New Show View All Shows 17 May 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 10 May 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 03 May 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 26 April 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 19 April 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 12 April 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 05 April 2026 - Carte Blanche HD Hi Lezanne [My Account] [Logout] Home Viewer Submissions Reports Contacts Music Cue Sheet Manage Users View Insert Edit Insert Insert Workflow Broken promises: Northern Cape By: Anina Peens | Commission Proposal Show: Carte Blanche One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): On the eve of the national election, we take a deep dive into the Northern Cape to look at what exactly the ANC government has done for the people. Unique Selling Point: How many broken buildings symbolise the governments' broken promises to its people? Summary: The Northern Cape... a forgotten province Further information: 1. Kimberley Water For over 20 years the Northern cape government has neglected to maintain the water system in Kimberley. Funding designated by national government was misused and mismanaged by both provincial and local government. The result? Knee high sewage running in people’s gardens and into their houses while drinking water is contaminated. Two wastewater treatment plants are completely rundown, and the entire system has now collapsed. While government is securing over 3.5 billion Rand to resurrect the system, private business has stepped in for the rescue. Last weekend, Ekapa, a private mining company began work on two of six earmarked projects to clean the clarifiers of the system and secure drinking water for the interim. 2. Hopeless Hopetown There seems to be countless unfinished projects in Hopetown. The community is fed up with local government that is never able to get anything done. The local sports stadium: Two years ago, over 12 million was granted to build a sports stadium for the use of the community. The contractor was awarded the tender, illegally and only spent 800 thousand of the 12 million on the stadium. Today, there is barely anything left of the stadium. It has been vandalized and even monkeys and baboons have moved and destroyed what is left of it. A forensic investigation was completed by treasury but the local government refuses to table it. Those responsible for the wasteful expenditure are still in office. The forensic report also investigated monies spent on the electrification of hillside, an informal settlement in Hopetown. People were moved to the settlement in 2014 and services were only given in 2018. But only partly… half of the community was left without electricity. Then came the 2021 elections and suddenly, it was a priority again. A contractor was awarded a tender to install electricity… but alas, a few poles were planted, without a proper spatial plan. There is no space for a proper road between the poles and there has been no electricity connected. After the election, the contractor was never seen again. The same culprits are implicated in the report and the ANC municipality refuses to table the report. 3. The De Aar Tunnels In 2019, the department of Northern cape department of agriculture was given over 20 million Rand to establish a community vegetable tunnel outside De Aar. Feasibility studies conducted prior to erecting the tunnels indicated that it the project had no feasibility. Yet, government continued. Now, five years down the line, the website boasts that the tunnels are providing tonnes of cherry tomatoes to the export market but to the contrary, the tunnels have been vandalized to the bone. There is nothing left but a few odd poles representing another broken promise to community members who hoped for employment in a province with one of the highest unemployment rates. And no one is taking responsibility… 4. Philipstown/Petrusville/ Keurtjieskloof - Another 12 million Rand given to a stadium that was never built in Keurtjieskloof. The contractor took off with the money and now baboons are living in the stadium while vandals are removing every last piece. - The town hall in Keurtjieskloof was also supposed to be upgraded for the use of the community… nothing has happened. - A brand-new school for Petrusville was initiated by premier Zimani Saul and millions were allocated for the project. Five years down the line and the school has still not been finished. - A state funded piggery was established for the community of Philipstown. Millions were spent, but there is not one pig left, just vandalized office buildings. - A contractor was hired two years ago to build a proper dumping site. He took two million Rand of the money and erected a windy house in an open field. That was it. Two years later, the same contractor was sworn in as municipal manager. It is alleged that he now sells sassa grants from his garage Extra Budget Items: Research and development: Three days prior to shoot: Accommodation and travel. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): On the eve of the national election, we take a deep dive into the Northern Cape to look at what exactly the ANC government has done for the people.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: How many broken buildings symbolise the governments' broken promises to its people?
metadata.Summary: The Northern Cape... a forgotten province
metadata.Further information: 1. Kimberley Water For over 20 years the Northern cape government has neglected to maintain the water system in Kimberley. Funding designated by national government was misused and mismanaged by both provincial and local government. The result? Knee high sewage running in people’s gardens and into their houses while drinking water is contaminated. Two wastewater treatment plants are completely rundown, and the entire system has now collapsed. While government is securing over 3.5 billion Rand to resurrect the system, private business has stepped in for the rescue. Last weekend, Ekapa, a private mining company began work on two of six earmarked projects to clean the clarifiers of the system and secure drinking water for the interim. 2. Hopeless Hopetown There seems to be countless unfinished projects in Hopetown. The community is fed up with local government that is never able to get anything done. The local sports stadium: Two years ago, over 12 million was granted to build a sports stadium for the use of the community. The contractor was awarded the tender, illegally and only spent 800 thousand of the 12 million on the stadium. Today, there is barely anything left of the stadium. It has been vandalized and even monkeys and baboons have moved and destroyed what is left of it. A forensic investigation was completed by treasury but the local government refuses to table it. Those responsible for the wasteful expenditure are still in office. The forensic report also investigated monies spent on the electrification of hillside, an informal settlement in Hopetown. People were moved to the settlement in 2014 and services were only given in 2018. But only partly… half of the community was left without electricity. Then came the 2021 elections and suddenly, it was a priority again. A contractor was awarded a tender to install electricity… but alas, a few poles were planted, without a proper spatial plan. There is no space for a proper road between the poles and there has been no electricity connected. After the election, the contractor was never seen again. The same culprits are implicated in the report and the ANC municipality refuses to table the report. 3. The De Aar Tunnels In 2019, the department of Northern cape department of agriculture was given over 20 million Rand to establish a community vegetable tunnel outside De Aar. Feasibility studies conducted prior to erecting the tunnels indicated that it the project had no feasibility. Yet, government continued. Now, five years down the line, the website boasts that the tunnels are providing tonnes of cherry tomatoes to the export market but to the contrary, the tunnels have been vandalized to the bone. There is nothing left but a few odd poles representing another broken promise to community members who hoped for employment in a province with one of the highest unemployment rates. And no one is taking responsibility… 4. Philipstown/Petrusville/ Keurtjieskloof - Another 12 million Rand given to a stadium that was never built in Keurtjieskloof. The contractor took off with the money and now baboons are living in the stadium while vandals are removing every last piece. - The town hall in Keurtjieskloof was also supposed to be upgraded for the use of the community… nothing has happened. - A brand-new school for Petrusville was initiated by premier Zimani Saul and millions were allocated for the project. Five years down the line and the school has still not been finished. - A state funded piggery was established for the community of Philipstown. Millions were spent, but there is not one pig left, just vandalized office buildings. - A contractor was hired two years ago to build a proper dumping site. He took two million Rand of the money and erected a windy house in an open field. That was it. Two years later, the same contractor was sworn in as municipal manager. It is alleged that he now sells sassa grants from his garage
